outcomes: Create valid, properly structured web pages using avariety of HTML features to form a typical 5-10 page site.

Apply programming principles to develop a fullyfunctioning and customized web site experience for boththe site user and site administrator.
Use JavaScript to enhance a web site’s interactivity usingthe DOM.
Use PHP to enhance a web site’s capabilities by creatingdata driven web page content, custom form validationand processing, and database manipulation using securemethodologies.

notes: The page heading is printed twice as CE1115 and once as CE934; the section was read as the single Web Master - Web Developer certificate. A reviewer may want to confirm which program code applies.
The 'Required Courses - Concentration' heading states 6.00 units, made up of two nested 'Select one of the following' choices. Each choice is recorded as its own block.
The 'Elective Courses - Concentration' heading states 6.00-7.00 units, made up of two nested 'Select one of the following' choices. Each choice is recorded as its own block.
The catalog prints codes with hyphens (e.g. CIS-72A). These were matched to closed-list codes without hyphens. CIS-56A was matched to the closed-list entry 'CIS56A'.
CSC-prefixed courses (CSC-14A, CSC-12, CSC-5, CSC-18A) are printed as separate rows in the choose-one lists, marked Historical. They were recorded as separate entries rather than as alternatives.
ADM-71A is not in the closed list and is marked as a catalog addition.
The outcomes are copied verbatim, including run-together words (e.g. 'avariety', 'anentire') that appear to come from line breaks lost in the source text.
The program description mentions emphases (graphics/animation vs. programming), but the requirements print a single course structure.
